identity.title: Bayesian-guided Label Mapping for Visual Reprogramming

problem.claim: Visual reprogramming must adapt pretrained-model interfaces when pretrained and downstream label sets differ.

gap.claim: Existing gradient-free one-to-one label mappings may miss complex relationships between pretrained and downstream labels.

contributions.claim: BLM builds an iteratively updated probabilistic label-mapping matrix whose entries quantify pairwise pretrained–downstream label relationships.
BLM provides a probabilistic lens for understanding and analyzing visual reprogramming effectiveness.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce Bayesian-guided label mapping that uses conditional probabilities and joint label distributions instead of restricting mappings to one-to-one correspondences.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments with pretrained vision models such as ResNeXt and vision-language models such as CLIP show BLM outperforming existing label-mapping methods.
The authors report that BLM's success supports a probabilistic analysis of visual reprogramming effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Visual reprogramming adapts pretrained vision-model interfaces for downstream tasks with potentially different labels.
One-to-one output label mappings are described as potentially overlooking complex pretrained–downstream label relationships.
BLM estimates an iteratively updated probabilistic mapping matrix using Bayesian conditional probabilities and joint distributions over downstream samples.
Experiments across vision and vision-language models are reported to show BLM outperforming existing mapping methods, while also motivating a probabilistic interpretation of VR.

source_observation.claim: The paper connects a limitation in the assumed mapping structure directly to a probabilistic matrix design and describes how the matrix is updated from joint label distributions.

lessons.interpretation: A precise failure mode can motivate both the representation and the evidence-generating mechanism of a proposed method.
lessons.application: When a baseline imposes a restrictive structural assumption, state the missed relationship explicitly and align the new representation and update rule with that relationship.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the restrictive assumption is required by the task or when the abstract provides no concrete basis for replacing it.

unknowns: The abstract gives no datasets, task details, quantitative results, statistical conditions, or definition of the compared existing methods.
It does not specify the exact Bayesian update procedure, computational cost, or whether the reported superiority holds uniformly across evaluated settings.
